note: Read by src-tauri/src/audio/drum_map.rs and src/audio/drum-map.test.ts so the Rust and TypeScript drum map rules cannot drift. `validity` cases say whether a mix carrying that `drumMap` must be accepted; `resolution` cases give, for a map and whether the track is percussion, the key each [key, articulation id or null] hit plays (null: no sound). `presets` cases give an embedded presets file and the presets that survive it: a preset that is malformed anywhere (its id, `rows` or one row) is dropped as a whole and reported, and the others survive, on both sides. `nativeOnly` holds forms that the native loader refuses and TypeScript cannot tell apart after JSON.parse: a number written as a float (38.0, 1e2) is an integer to JSON.parse, so only the native loader (the loader of record) can refuse it; the persisted writer never writes one. TypeScript's test pins that it reads each as the integer, so the difference stays exactly this list. `files` cases give the bytes of a drum map file (its `text`, or its `hex`, padded with spaces to `padTo` bytes when that is given) and either the code of the first thing wrong with it (`error`) or what an import reads from it (`imported`: name, base, rows); read by src-tauri/src/drum_map_file.rs and src/audio/drum-map-file.test.ts.
